title: Worksheet 14: Model-View-Controller (MVC)
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Model-View-Controller, or MVC, is a pattern that splits an app into three parts, each with its own job. The Model holds the data and the rules, such as a student's score in a quiz game. The View is what the user sees on the screen, such as the score displayed in a bubble. The Controller listens to what the user does, such as clicking a button, and tells the Model to change. When the Model changes, the View is updated to show the new data. For example, when a player clicks "Answer," the Controller tells the Model to add 10 points, and then the View redraws the score on the screen. Because the parts are separate, a designer can change the View from a bubble to a bar without touching the Model, and the rules in the Model do not change.

questions.text: In MVC, what does the Model hold?

questions.correct: What the user sees on the screen
distractors: The part that listens to clicks

questions.correct: Listens to what the user does and tells the Model to change
distractors: Draws the score on the screen

A programmer changes the quiz rule so each correct answer is worth 20 points instead of 10. Based on the paragraph, which statement is correct?
questions.correct: The Model holds the rule, and the View's design can stay the same
distractors: The View holds the rule, so the design must be rebuilt
The Controller holds the rule, so the Model must be rewritten
